ground_truth_note: The claim that cooked rice must be thrown out after 24 hours is inaccurate. According to the USDA and food safety experts, cooked rice is safe to eat for 3 to 4 days if it is refrigerated promptly and stored properly. http://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety
note_text: Cooked rice doesn't need to be thrown out after 24 hours. When refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking, it stays safe for 3-6 days. The 2-hour rule applies to room temperature, not refrigerated storage. https://www.usarice.com/thinkrice/discover-rice/how-to-store-rice
search_results:
The claim that you must throw rice out after 24 hours is **incorrect**. Cooked rice can be safely stored in the refrigerator for significantly longer than one day.

According to food safety guidelines, **cooked rice can be refrigerated for 3–6 days**[1][2][3]. The USA Rice organization recommends storage for three to five days[2], while Mahatma Rice and Riceland Foods extend this to up to six days[1][3]. The key safety requirement is that cooked rice must be **refrigerated within two hours** of cooking to prevent bacterial growth[1][2], not discarded after 24 hours.

If you want to keep cooked rice longer, it can also be **frozen for up to 6–8 months**[2][3][4].

The confusion may stem from the important two-hour rule: rice should never sit at room temperature for more than two hours[1][2], as this creates conditions for harmful bacteria to develop. However, once properly refrigerated, rice remains safe and maintains good quality for multiple days.
